artifact: M9 South Fork padded low-relief solver foam V219 review
summary: V219 removes independently admitted half-triangles from the one-metre South Fork solver-foam overlay, admits only complete paired quads inside wet/deep hydraulic support, and retains two transparent support cells around active foam so a mesh diagonal cannot define the visible edge. Overlay separation is reduced from the V218 0.56 m control to a 0.14 m cap above the existing broad-water micro-relief. In the exact V218/V219 comparison, Meat Grinder's long bright polygon ribbons become lower irregular foam patches; Troublemaker retains sparse solver-authorized foam; and no new bank overlap is visible at Coloma Bridge or the other fixed views. This is a material presentation improvement, but the coarse terrain, flat water body, repeated vegetation, generic lighting, and absent named external approvals still fail the full photoreal acceptance gate.

implementation.material_mask: project-owned flow-aligned foam lace multiplied by solver-derived vertex opacity and runtime raft/crew exclusion

objective_capture_comparison.method: exact fixed cameras after consecutive water-only regenerations; changed pixels use maximum RGB delta greater than 8

review_decision.reason: The complete-quad topology removes mesh-diagonal admission, and the shallow separation removes the most legible raised polygon fins while keeping the solver-authorized whitewater field readable.

rejected_experiments: V217 static breaking-wave sheets: rejected because the added bright slanted polygons worsened Troublemaker and were unreadable at Meat Grinder and Coloma.

V218 complete-quad topology at the legacy 0.56 m overlay displacement: retained only as a matched technical control because it removed half-triangle admission but left long bright raised facet silhouettes.

The 30 m/derived terrain and shoreline remain broad and visibly procedural at guide-eye distance.
Tree crowns, ground cover, bridge detail, distant relief, lighting, and atmosphere do not yet match an approved photographic reference set.
